title: Europeana Project Month 2026 launches in November
content:
Europeana Project Month 2026 is a series of webinars on the topic of the data space in practice: tools, impact and synergies broadcast during November.

Consisting of 14 projects that Europeana is actively involved in, ECHOES, INFINITY and ECHOLOT will feature in the webinar “Bridging the data space and the ECCCH” and HERITALISE in the webinar “3D Digitisation“.

ECHOES: Building the Cultural Heritage Cloud ecosystem will introduce the project, present the latest progress achieved by ECHOES, and demonstrate how the project is building an open, federated ecosystem that connects institutions, datasets, tools and expertise across Europe. A key focus will be on the relationship between the Cultural Heritage Cloud and the Common European Data Space for Cultural Heritage.

Organised by the Europeana Foundation, the webinars will run every Tuesday and Thursday during November over two sessions:

  • Morning sessions (09:30-12:00 CET)
  • Afternoon sessions (14:00-16:00 CET)

    • Participation is free but registration is required. More information is available on the Data Space website.

title: First ECHOES training course launched on DARIAH-CAMPUS
content:
ECHOES has launched its first training course! Introduction to European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage aims to build learners’ foundational understanding of the key concepts and technologies necessary to engage with the Cultural Heritage Cloud. The course, available on DARIAH Campus, consists of  five units which provide the background to the development of the ECCCH, the key concepts, how collaboration works in the ECCCH, Open Science and FAIR principles and concludes with a set of illustrative scenarios.

An extract from Unit 2: Key Concepts and Foundations

In addition, ECHOES has also developed the OntoMatchGame to facilitate learning about ontological models. This educational application is in the form of a card game, providing a step-by-step guide to understanding how the ontology works and how mapping is used to associate data with ontology entities.

The training course and OntoMatchGame can both be accessed through the Capacity Building page where further information is also available.

title: Seven more “Engagement and Collaboration” projects started
content:
ECHOES is pleased to announce that a further seven projects funded by the Cascading Grants programme under Call 2, “Engagement and Collaboration” have started.

The Call invited applications from Cultural Heritage institutions (CHIs) to help raise awareness of the Cultural Heritage Cloud and grow its community, to support skills development and capacity building, with a focus on small and medium-sized CHIs. A variety of approaches was encouraged such as training seminars, help desks, promotional materials along with applicants own proposals. Further details about all the projects are to be found on the Second Call Awards page.

The seven new projects:

Heritage in Motion
Scope: Provide training and toolkits for Audiovisual (AV) collections, organise a symposium to share practices and build the ECCCH AV community.
Geographic region(s): Pan-Europe
Target organisations: AV heritage institutions.

EMPOWER-CH
Scope: Dissemination, consultation and peer- exchange activities to make the ECCCH more accessible to museum and GLAM professionals.
Geographic region(s): Italy, pan-Europe
Target organisations: Museums and cultural heritage institutions.
snippet: ECHOES is pleased to announce that a further seven projects funded by the Cascading Grants programme under Call 2, “Engagement and Collaboration” have started.

title: SSH Open Marketplace training series session for GLAMS featuring ECHOES
content:
DARIAH is organising a session dedicated to GLAM audiences on Friday, the 18th of September where ECHOES will be prominently featured by Giorgia Lo Nigro from CNRS. This is as part of the 2026 SSH Open Marketplace training series.

Cultural heritage collections held by galleries, libraries, archives and museums (GLAM) are a cornerstone of arts and humanities research — but working with them brings its own data challenges, from fragmented standards to the gap between “metadata” and the real workflows researchers need to reuse this material responsibly.

This session is part of the SSH Open Marketplace Training Series 2026, an eight-part series of online hands-on workshops organised by the SSH Open Marketplace Editorial Board to strengthen FAIR and digital research competencies, following the FAIR-by-design methodology developed in skills4EOSC. This sixth session, “Thematic: GLAM institutions,” brings together speakers from the ECHOES project, the SSH Open Marketplace and ETH Zurich Library to look at cultural heritage and GLAM data specifically.

title: Call for papers for the EUROGRAPHICS Workshop open until 31st July
content:
GCH 2026 has extended its Call for Papers (short and long) for the special track on the ECCCH, “Visual Computing in the Context of the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage” to the 31st July.

GCH 2026 (https://gch2026.virvig.eu/) serves as a premier forum for experts from both the ICT and Cultural Heritage (CH) sectors. The workshop aims to showcase how computer graphics, AI, and digital technologies are revolutionising the research, preservation, and dissemination of cultural heritage. We particularly encourage interdisciplinary submissions that foster collaboration between researchers, heritage professionals, and creative industries.

Date: This year’s event will be held from November 2nd to November 5th, 2026.
Location & Venue:  The workshop is hosted by the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) in the vibrant city of Barcelona, Spain.
Organisation: GCH 2026 is organised by the ViRVIG Research Centre (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya) and supported by Eurographics.

ECCCH Track: Visual Computing in the Context of the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH)

title: AUTOMATA Archaeological Technologies Survey published
content:
The AUTOMATA consortium has published the final report of its international survey on the practices and perceptions of archaeological professionals regarding the technologies explored by the project: 3D modelling, non-destructive archaeometry, artificial intelligence and robotics.

Coordinated by the Institut national de recherches archéologiques préventives (Inrap), the survey gathered 323 responses from 42 countries between March and May 2025. Respondents were mainly active in academic research and archaeology, and showed varying degrees of familiarity with the technologies addressed, from widespread knowledge and use of 3D modelling to more limited experience with robotics.

The report highlights that 3D modelling is already widely used in archaeological practice, especially through photogrammetry, while non-destructive archaeometry is mainly applied to material characterisation, including soils and ceramics. In both areas, respondents identified lack of training, cost, access to equipment and data storage as key obstacles to wider adoption.

title: KINETIKA’s first newsletter published
content:
The KINETIKA project have published their first newsletter which provides a comprehensive overview of their objectives and activities since starting in January.

Catch up with the goals of the project and the five pilot studies, the consortium members and kick-off meeting as well as the joint webinar held with MusicSphere.

  • Download the PDF version.
  • Subscribe to the KINETIKA newsletter.

    • About KINETIKA
    KINETIKA embraces Industry 4.0 concepts to create a groundbreaking 4D digital twin modular framework for cultural heritage objects with mechanical parts, focusing on movable structures of industrial heritage and cultural heritage (CH) masonry. The project will validate its innovations through representative case studies, including clock towers, looms and drawbridges, demonstrating the platform’s adaptability and guiding further applications across a wide range of cultural artefacts.

title: MusicSphere progresses with the Hydraulis of Dion Use Case
content:
The MusicSphere consortium met in early June in Thessaloniki, Greece, to start work on the first Use Case – the Hydraulis of Dion.

The meeting started with a trip to Katerini to visit the Greek Evangelical Church, home to the largest pipe organ installed within a church in Greece. The partners were given a guided tour and a live demonstration of the organ by Giannis Adamidis.  The visit provided consortium members with valuable insights into the preservation, performance, and cultural significance of pipe organs, which remain a central focus of the project.

Original Hydraulis of Dion (left) and the reconstruction by the International Hellenic University (right)

title: Infinity project members win two best paper awards
content:
Infinity project members have made quite an impact in the Cultural Heritage community by winning two best paper awards!

The first paper, “Cultural Heritage Survey: an Ontology Design Pattern” was awarded the Best SEMDH Paper at the Third International Workshop of Semantic Digital Humanities which was held as part of the 23rd European Semantic Web Conference (ESWC) held on the 10th-14th May in Dubrovnik, Croatia. This paper paper introduces the Cultural Heritage Survey Ontology Design Pattern (CHS-ODP), a content pattern that abstracts from specific implementations and provides a reference core for modelling survey processes within cultural heritage knowledge graphs. Further information on the Infinity website.

Three days later, a second award, Best Resource Paper, was given to “Bench4KE: Benchmarking Automated Competency Question Generation” by the ESWC which addresses the evaluation of LLM-based methods and tools that generate Competency Questions posed by Ontologists through Bench4KE, an extensible API-based benchmarking system forKnowledge Engineering automation. Further information on the Infinity website.
